name: gstack-execution
description: v0.24.0: XE-011, one vocabulary. references/vocabulary.json is a SKOS concept scheme holding every outcome, item status, severity, disposition and round-record shape the dispatcher enforces; peer_review.py loads them from it instead of restating literals, ReviewError refuses an outcome the vocabulary does not define, and packets and rounds record the vocabulary version so verify can report drift. vocab_check.py fails on an item status outside the vocabulary or a definition restated in a contract. v0.23.0: the execution-economy objective (XE-001..010) and the evidence items that carry it. A packet whose acceptance criteria are narrower than the item they claim does not open a review: packet_coverage.mjs scores each declared criterion against the packet and cmd_open refuses a packet that leaves one uncovered unless --accept-narrow-packet is passed, which is recorded as an override rather than as a pass. The gate is monotonic -- a score may raise a gate and never lower one -- and a scorer that did not run is recorded as not run, never as coverage verified. Scoring stays out of the dispatcher: coverage_verdict reads a report and never produces one. The E2E gate proves it can run before anything is pushed (preflight, endform_workflow.py). Capability grants name what they permit, not who may act. Tool order is connector, then CLI, then REST, then browser, with tool_rung.py answering 'is there a connector for this?' by looking rather than by eyeballing a tool list. Cross-tool review is batched per checkpoint and dispatched rather than blocked on. Reviewer routing is a table of {family, model, floor}: a reviewer sharing the builder's model family is refused before it runs, a fallback is recorded as one, and a truncated or empty response is distinguishable from a malformed one. The repository runs its own checks on every pull request, and a run discovering zero checks fails rather than passing. A reviewer receives the diff, the files it changes and the code that references them -- not the repository tree -- which took a review that had been timing out down to 67 seconds, and the surface names the callers the change did not touch. review_host.sh stands up a shell where a dispatched review survives between calls. A round records which files the reviewer opened, how many it was offered, and whether it looked beyond the diff; a filesystem that cannot report reads says so rather than reporting a review that examined nothing. Peer-review records must be written to a declared durable directory: the old default wrote them to a session-local home, so review IDs cited as evidence resolved to nothing.
